paragraphs: AMERISAFE, Inc. is a specialty provider of workers' compensation insurance focused on small to mid-sized employers engaged in hazardous industries, principally construction, trucking, logging and lumber, agriculture, services, manufacturing, and maritime. Since commencing operations in 1986, we have gained significant experience underwriting the complex workers' compensation exposures inherent in these industries. We provide coverage to employers under state and federal workers' compensation laws. These laws prescribe wage replacement and medical care benefits that employers are obligated to provide to their employees who are injured in the course and scope of their employment. Our workers' compensation insurance policies provide benefits to injured employees for, among other things, temporary or permanent disability, death and medical and hospital expenses. The benefits payable and the duration of those benefits are set by state or federal law. The benefits vary by jurisdiction, the nature and severity of the injury and the wages of the employee. The employer, who is the policyholder, pays the premiums for coverage.

Hazardous industry employers tend to have less frequent but more severe claims, as compared to employers in other industries, due to the nature of their businesses. Injuries that occur are often severe in nature including death, dismemberment, paraplegia and quadriplegia. As a result, employers engaged in hazardous industries pay substantially higher than average rates for workers' compensation insurance compared to employers in other industries, as measured per payroll dollar. The higher premium rates are due to the nature of the work performed and the inherent workplace danger of our target policyholders.

We employ a proactive, disciplined approach to underwriting employers and providing comprehensive services intended to lessen the overall incidence and cost of workplace injuries. We provide safety services at employers' workplaces as a vital component of our underwriting process and to promote safer workplaces. We utilize proactive claims management practices that we believe ultimately reduce the overall cost of our claims. In addition, our premium audit services calculate the appropriate premiums for our policyholders under the terms of their policies and enable us to monitor payroll patterns that cause underwriting, safety or fraud concerns.

We believe that the higher rates typically paid by our policyholders, together with our disciplined underwriting, safety, claims, and audit services, provide us with the opportunity to earn attractive returns on equity.

We are an insurance holding company, incorporated in Texas in 1985. We began operations in 1986 by focusing on workers' compensation insurance for logging contractors in the southeast U.S. Beginning in 1994, we expanded our focus to include the other hazardous industries we serve today. Two of our three insurance subsidiaries, American Interstate Insurance Company (AIIC) and Silver Oak Casualty, Inc. (SOCI), are domiciled in Nebraska. Our other insurance subsidiary, American Interstate Insurance Company of Texas (AIICTX), is domiciled in Texas. All three insurance subsidiaries carry an A.M. Best rating of "A" (Excellent).
The terms "AMERISAFE," the "Company," "we," "us" or "our" refer to AMERISAFE, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries, as the context requires.
We believe we have the following competitive advantages:

Focus on Hazardous Industries. We have extensive experience insuring employers engaged in certain hazardous industries and have a history of profitably underwriting these industries. Our specialized knowledge of these hazardous industries helps us better serve our policyholders, which leads to greater policyholder loyalty and policy retention. Our policy renewal rate on voluntary business that we elected to quote for renewal was 93.1% in 2025.

Focus on Small to Mid-Sized Employers. We believe large insurance companies generally do not target small to mid-sized employers in certain hazardous industries due to their smaller premium sizes, types of operations, mobile workforces and extensive service needs. We provide these employers enhanced services, including premium payment plans to better match premium payments with our policyholders' payroll costs and cash flow.

Knowledgeable, Dedicated Employees. We deliver an exceptional product with integrity through professional, knowledgeable and dedicated employees. Service is a distinguishing factor for us and the level of that service is dependent on the expertise and caring culture of our employees.

Specialized Underwriting Expertise. Based on our 40-year history of insuring employers engaged in hazardous industries, we have developed industry specific risk analysis and rating tools that support our underwriters in risk selection and pricing. We are highly disciplined when quoting and binding new and renewal business. We do not delegate underwriting authority to agencies, marketers or to any other third parties that sell our insurance.

Comprehensive Safety Services. We provide proactive safety reviews of employers' worksites, which are often located in rural areas. These safety reviews are a vital component of our underwriting process and also assist our policyholders in loss prevention, and encourage safer workplaces by deploying experienced field safety professionals (FSPs) to our policyholders' worksites. In 2025, 93.4% of our new voluntary business policyholders had pre-quotation safety inspections. Additionally, we perform periodic on-site safety surveys for our voluntary business policyholders as well as other services discussed below under "Safety".

Proactive Claims Management. Our employees manage substantially all of our claims in-house, utilizing intensive claims management practices that emphasize a personalized approach, as well as quality, cost-effective medical treatment. As of December 31, 2025, open indemnity claims per field case manager (FCM) averaged 51 claims, which we believe is significantly less than the industry average. We also believe our claims management practices allow us to achieve a more favorable claim outcome, accelerate an employee's return to work, lessen the likelihood of litigation and more rapidly close claims, all of which ultimately lead to lower overall claim costs.

Efficient Operating Platform. Through cost management initiatives, we maintain one of the more efficient operations in the workers' compensation industry. In 2025, our expense ratio was 30.4%. We believe that our expense ratio is generally lower than that of our competitors, which gives us a greater opportunity to generate underwriting profit.

Risks Related to Regulation and Litigation
We are subject to extensive state and federal regulations, and legislation, and any changes in such regulations or laws may negatively impact our business.
Assessments and premium surcharges for state guaranty funds, second injury funds and other mandatory pooling arrangements may reduce our profitability.
Legal or other administrative proceedings could have a material adverse effect on our operations or results of operations.
We may have exposure to losses from terrorism for which we are required by law to provide coverage.
If we are unable to obtain reinsurance on favorable terms, our ability to write policies could be adversely affected.
A downgrade in the A.M. Best rating of one or more of our significant reinsurers could adversely affect our financial condition.
If any of our current reinsurers were to terminate participation in our reinsurance treaty program, we could be exposed to an increased risk of loss.
We may not be able to recover amounts due from our reinsurers, which would adversely affect our financial condition.
Risks Related to Our Common Stock
Our revenues and results of operations may fluctuate as a result of factors beyond our control, which may cause the price of our common stock to be volatile.
The trading price of our common stock may decline.
Securities analysts may discontinue coverage of our common stock or may issue negative reports about us, which may adversely affect the trading price of our common stock.
Future sales of our common stock may affect the trading price of our common stock.

In general, the premium rates for our insurance policies are established when coverage is initiated and, therefore, before all of the underlying costs are known. Like other workers' compensation insurance companies, we rely on estimates and assumptions in setting our premium rates. Establishing adequate rates is necessary to generate sufficient revenue to offset losses, loss adjustment expenses and other underwriting expenses, and to earn an underwriting profit. If we fail to accurately assess the risks, we may fail to charge adequate premium rates to cover our losses and expenses, which could reduce our net income and cause us to become unprofitable. For example, when initiating coverage on a new policyholder, we estimate future claims expense based, in part, on prior claims information provided by the policyholder's previous insurance carriers. If this prior claims information is not accurate, we may underprice our policy by using claims estimates that are too low. paragraphs: Gross Premiums Written. Gross premiums written for 2025 were $313.9 million, compared to $294.1 million for 2024, an increase of 6.7%. The increase was attributable to a $27.1 million increase in annual premiums on voluntary policies written during the period, driven mostly by a 10.2% increase in in-force policy count. This increase was partially offset by a $7.6 million decrease in premiums resulting from payroll audits and related premium adjustments for policies written in previous periods.

Net Premiums Written. Net premiums written for 2025 were $296.6 million, compared to $276.0 million for 2024, an increase of 7.5%. The increase was primarily attributable to the increase in gross premiums written. As a percentage of gross premiums earned, ceded premiums were 5.7% for 2025 compared to 6.3% for 2024. Ceded premiums decreased as we purchased levels of reinsurance coverage at generally lower prices in 2025. For additional information, see Item 1, "Business—Reinsurance."

Net Premiums Earned. Net premiums earned for 2025 were $283.1 million, compared to $270.6 million for 2024, an increase of 4.6%. The increase was primarily attributable to the increase in net premiums written.

Net Investment Income. Net investment income in 2025 was $27.0 million, a decrease of 7.6% from the $29.2 million reported in 2024. The decrease was due to lower average invested asset balances in the period compared to prior year. Average invested assets, including cash and cash equivalents, decreased 8.2%, from an average of $890.4 million for 2024 to an average of $817.2 million for 2025. The average pre-tax net investment yield on our investment portfolio was 3.3% per annum for 2025, compared to 3.4% per annum for 2024. The year-end tax-equivalent yield on our investment portfolio was 3.8% per annum for both 2025 and 2024. The tax-equivalent yield is calculated using the effective interest rate and the appropriate marginal tax rate.

Net Realized Gains (Losses) on Investments. Net realized gains on investments in 2025 totaled $3.0 million compared to net realized losses on investments of $0.6 million in 2024. In 2025, net realized gains on investments resulted primarily from the sale of equity and fixed maturity securities classified as available-for-sale as well as the redemption of fixed maturity securities. In 2024, net realized losses on investments resulted primarily from the sale of equity and fixed maturity securities classified as available-for-sale as well as the redemption of fixed maturity securities.
Net Unrealized Gains on Equity Securities. Net unrealized gains on equity securities in 2025 were $3.7 million compared to net unrealized gains on equity securities of $9.5 million in 2024.

Loss and Loss Adjustment Expenses Incurred. Loss and LAE incurred totaled $169.9 million for 2025, compared to $157.3 million for 2024, an increase of $12.7 million, or 8.1%. The current accident year losses and LAE incurred were $203.8 million, or 72.0% of net premiums earned, compared to $192.2 million, or 71.0% of net premiums earned for 2024. The Company increased the 2025 accident year loss ratio from 71% to 72% largely due to the frequency of severity observed in accident year 2025 compared with prior accident years. We recorded favorable prior accident year development of $33.9 million in 2025, compared to $34.9 million in 2024. This is discussed in more detail below in "Prior Year Development." Our net loss ratio was 60.0% for 2025 and 58.1% for 2024.

Underwriting and Certain Other Operating Costs, Commissions and Salaries and Benefits. Underwriting and certain other operating costs, commissions and salaries and benefits for 2025 were $86.0 million, compared to $80.1 million for 2024. The increase was primarily due to a $3.1 million increase in insurance related assessments, a $1.5 million increase in compensation expense, a $1.3 million increase in commission expense and a $0.5 million increase in accounts receivable write-offs. Partially offsetting these amounts were a $0.9 million decrease in professional fees and a $0.6 million decrease in taxes and fees. Our underwriting expense ratio increased to 30.4% in 2025 from 29.6% in 2024.
Income tax expense. Income tax expense for 2025 was $11.7 million, compared to $13.6 million for 2024. The effective tax rate was 19.9% for 2025 and 19.7% for 2024.

paragraphs: AMERISAFE, Inc. 為專門提供勞工補償保險的公司，主要服務小型至中型僱主，這些僱主從事高風險產業，包括建設、貨運、伐木與木材、農業、服務、製造及海運。自1986年開始營運以來，我們已累積豐富的經驗，以處理這些產業中複雜的勞工補償風險。我們為僱主提供符合州及聯邦勞工補償法規的保障。這些法規規定僱主必須為其員工在職務範圍內受傷時提供工資替代與醫療照護福利。我們的勞工補償保險政策為受傷員工提供福利，包括暫時或永久傷殘、死亡及醫療與住院費用。支付的福利及持續時間由州或聯邦法規所規定。福利因管轄區域、傷勢性質與嚴重程度及員工工資而有所不同。僱主為政策持有人，需支付保費以取得保障。
高風險產業僱主的聲請通常較少但較嚴重，與其他產業的僱主相比。發生的傷害往往性質嚴重，包括死亡、斷肢、截癱及四肢癱瘓。因此，從事高風險產業的僱主為勞工補償保險支付的費用，相比其他產業的僱主，每美元薪資的費用顯著更高。較高的保費是因為工作的性質及我們目標政策持有人的工作場所固有的危險性所致。
我們採用積極且嚴謹的承保方式，為僱主提供全面的服務，以降低工作場所傷害的總體發生率與成本。我們在僱主的工作場所提供安全服務，作為我們承保流程的重要組成部分，並促進更安全的工作環境。我們運用積極的聲請管理作法，我們認為這最終會降低我們聲請的總體成本。此外，我們的保費稽核服務會根據政策條款計算適當的保費，並使我們能監測導致承保、安全或詐欺疑慮的薪資模式。
我們認為，我們的政策持有人通常支付較高的費用，加上我們嚴謹的承保、安全、聲請及稽核服務，使我們有機會在權益上獲得有吸引力的回報。

我們是一家保險控股公司，於1985年在德克薩斯州註冊成立。我們於1986年開始營運，專注於美國南部的伐木承包商的勞工補償保險。自1994年起，我們擴展業務範疇，包括今天所服務的其他高風險產業。我們的三個保險子公司中的兩個，美國國際保險公司（AIIC）與銀橡樹意外保險公司（SOCI），註冊地點為內布拉斯加州。我們的另一個保險子公司，美國國際保險公司德克薩斯分公司（AIICTX），註冊地點為德克薩斯州。所有三個保險子公司均獲得A.M. Best評級為"A"（優秀）。
「AMERISAFE」、「公司」、「我們」、「我們」或「我們的」均指AMERISAFE, Inc.及其合併子公司，視語境而定。
我們認為我們擁有以下競爭優勢：
專注於高風險產業。我們擁有豐富的經驗，為從事特定高風險產業的僱主提供保險，並有歷史紀錄顯示這些產業的承保獲利。我們對這些高風險產業的專業知識有助於我們更好地服務政策持有人，這導致政策持有人的忠誠度與留存率更高。我們在2025年選擇續保的自願業務的續保率為93.1%。
著重於中小型僱主。我們認為大型保險公司通常不會針對某些危險產業的中小型僱主進行目標行銷，因為這些僱主的保費規模較小、作業類型、流動性勞工以及廣泛的服務需求等因素。我們為這些僱主提供增強的服務，包括保費分期付款方案，以更好地匹配保費支付與我們被保險人的薪資成本及現金流。
具專業知識且忠誠的員工。我們透過專業、具知識且忠誠的員工，以誠信的方式提供卓越的產品。服務是我們的區辨特質，而服務的水準則取決於員工的專業知識與關懷文化。
專門的核保專業知識。根據我們40年的經驗，為從事危險產業的僱主提供保險，我們已發展出產業特定的風險分析與評價工具，以支援我們核保人員在風險選擇與定價上的決策。我們在報價與承保新業務及續保業務時，具有高度的紀律。我們不會將核保權限委託給經紀公司、行銷人員或其他銷售我們保險的第三方。

全面的安全服務。我們提供主動的安全評估，評估僱主的工作場所，這些場所通常位於鄉村地區。這些安全評估是我們核保流程中的重要組成部分，同時也協助我們的被保險人進行損失預防，並透過派遣經驗豐富的現場安全專業人員（FSPs）至我們被保險人的工作場所，鼓勵更安全的工作環境。2025年，我們新加入的自願性業務被保險人中，有93.4%進行了報價前的安全檢查。此外，我們也會為自願性業務被保險人進行定期的現場安全檢查，以及下列在「安全」部分所討論的其他服務。
主動的理賠管理。我們的員工基本上處理我們所有的理賠案件，並運用強調個別化方式、品質及成本效益的理賠管理作法。截至2025年12月31日，每位現場理賠經理（FCM）平均處理51件開放式的賠償案件，我們認為這顯著低於產業平均值。我們也認為，我們的理賠管理作法使我們能獲得更優良的理賠結果，加速員工重返工作，降低訴訟的可能性，並更快地結案，這些最終都會導致整體理賠成本降低。
高效的運營平台。透過成本管理措施，我們維持工災保險產業中較為高效的運營。2025年，我們的費用率為30.4%。我們認為，我們的費用率通常低於競爭對手，這使我們有更大的機會產生承保利潤。

paragraphs: 毛利率寫入金額。2025 年毛利率寫入金額為 313.9 百萬美元，較 2024 年的 294.1 百萬美元增加 6.7%。此增加主要係因於本期間內所寫入的自願性保單年金增加 27.1 百萬美元，主要驅動因素為在力保單數量增加 10.2%。此增加部分抵銷因薪資稽核及相關保費調整，導致先前期間所寫入保單的保費減少 7.6 百萬美元。

淨毛 Premiums Written。2025 年淨毛 Premiums Written 為 296.6 百萬美元，較 2024 年的 276.0 百萬美元增加 7.5%。此增加主要係因於毛 Premiums Written 的增加。以毛 Premiums 獲得為基準，2025 年讓渡 Premiums 佔比為 5.7%，較 2024 年的 6.3% 降低。讓渡 Premiums 減少係因於 2025 年我們購買的再保險覆蓋範圍較低價格。有關更多資訊，請參閱第 1 項 "業務—再保險。"
淨毛 Premiums Earned。2025 年淨毛 Premiums Earned 為 283.1 百萬美元，較 2024 年的 270.6 百萬美元增加 4.6%。此增加主要係因於淨毛 Premiums Written 的增加。

淨投資收入。2025 年淨投資收入為 27.0 百萬美元，較 2024 年的 29.2 百萬美元減少 7.6%。此減少係因於本期間平均投資資產餘額較前一年為低。平均投資資產餘額（包括現金及現金等價物）減少 8.2%，從 2024 年平均 890.4 百萬美元降至 2025 年平均 817.2 百萬美元。2025 年投資組合的平均預稅淨投資報酬率為 3.3% 年，較 2024 年的 3.4% 年為低。2025 年及 2024 年投資組合的年底稅後報酬率均為 3.8% 年。稅後報酬率係以有效利率及適當的邊際稅率計算。
投資淨實現損益。2025 年投資淨實現收益為 3.0 百萬美元，較 2024 年的投資淨實現損失 0.6 百萬美元為高。2025 年投資淨實現收益主要來自於出售被歸類為可供出售的股權及固定收益證券，以及固定收益證券的贖回。2024 年投資淨實現損失主要來自於出售被歸類為可供出售的股權及固定收益證券，以及固定收益證券的贖回。
股權證券淨未實現收益。2025 年股權證券淨未實現收益為 3.7 百萬美元，較 2024 年的股權證券淨未實現收益 9.5 百萬美元為低。

損失及損失調整費用發生。2025 年損失及損失調整費用發生總計為 169.9 百萬美元，較 2024 年的 157.3 百萬美元增加 12.7 百萬美元，或增加 8.1%。2025 年當年度事故年損失及損失調整費用發生為 203.8 百萬美元，或佔淨毛 Premiums Earned 的 72.0%，較 2024 年的 192.2 百萬美元，或佔淨毛 Premiums Earned 的 71.0%。本公司將 2025 年事故年損失比率從 71% 提高至 72%，主要係因於 2025 年事故年嚴重程度頻率較前一年事故年為高。我們在 2025 年記錄了有利的前一年事故年發展 33.9 百萬美元，較 2024 年的 34.9 百萬美元為低。此內容在下文 "前一年發展" 中有更詳細說明。我們 2025 年的淨損失比率為 60.0%，而 2024 年為 58.1%。

保險及某些其他營運費用、佣金及薪資與福利。2025 年保險及某些其他營運費用、佣金及薪資與福利為 86.0 百萬美元，較 2024 年的 80.1 百萬美元增加。此增加主要係因於保險相關評估增加 3.1 百萬美元、薪資費用增加 1.5 百萬美元、佣金費用增加 1.3 百萬美元及應收款寫銷增加 0.5 百萬美元。部分抵銷這些金額的是專業費用減少 0.9 百萬美元及稅費與費用減少 0.6 百萬美元。我們 2025 年的保險費用比率提高至 30.4%，較 2024 年的 29.6% 為高。
所得稅費用。2025 年的所得稅費用為 11.7 百萬美元，與 2024 年的 13.6 百萬美元相比。2025 年的有效稅率為 19.9%，2024 年為 19.7%。

headings: 若我們未能適當建立 premium rates，將會對我們的營運成果造成不利影響。
若我們無法實現投資目標，將可能對我們的財務狀況及營運成果造成不利影響。
我們的損失準備金係基於估計值，可能不足以覆蓋我們實際的損失。
我們未來可能需要額外資金，該資金可能無法取得，或僅能在不利條件下取得。
工傷保險產業屬週期性產業，可能影響我們整體的財務表現。
我們營運於高度競爭的產業，僅提供單一類型的保險產品，且競爭對手可能擁有較多的財務資源，這些因素均可能影響我們有效競爭的能力。
若我們無法維持與獨立機構的關係，我們可能無法以獲利方式營運。
新興聲請與保障問題對我們業務的影響尚屬不確定。
我們的 A.M. Best 等級若遭降級，將可能減少我們所能承保的業務量。
科技外泄或系統故障，包括因惡意網路攻擊導致我們、保單持有人或服務提供者之問題，可能幹擾或以其他方式對我們業務造成負面影響。
我們員工的專業能力、身心健康與韌性，是維持我們在高風險勞工補償產業中競爭優勢所必需的。
我們的業務依賴我們的高階主管，因其產業專業知識、對我們市場的瞭解以及與銷售我們保險之獨立機構的關係。
若無法有效管理我們的營運，將使我們難以競爭，並可能影響我們以獲利方式營運的能力。
與規範及訴訟相關的風險
本公司受美國聯邦及州政府嚴格規範與立法管制，任何相關規範或法律的變更可能對本公司業務造成負面影響。
各州保證基金、第二傷害基金及其他強制性共保安排的評估與 premium surcharges 可能降低本公司利潤。
法律或其他行政程序可能對本公司營運或營運成果造成重大不利影響。
本公司可能因恐怖攻擊而面臨損失，且依法需提供相關保險 coverage。
與再保險商相關的風險
若本公司無法以有利條件取得再保險，可能影響本公司銷售保單的能力。
若本公司任一重要再保險商的 A.M. Best 等級遭降級，可能對本公司財務狀況造成不利影響。
若本公司現有任一再保險商終止參與再保險協議計畫，本公司可能面臨更高的損失風險。
我們可能無法從再保險公司收回應收金額，這將不利於我們的財務狀況。
與我們普通股相關的風險
我們的營業收入及營運成果可能因超出我們控制範圍的因素而波動，這可能導致我們普通股的價格波動。
我們普通股的交易價格可能下跌。
證券分析師可能停止覆蓋我們的普通股，或發布對我們不利的報告，這可能不利於我們普通股的交易價格。
未來我們普通股的銷售可能影響普通股的交易價格。

前瞻性陳述為所有非歷史事實之陳述。您不應過度依賴這些陳述。本公司不負有任何更新任何前瞻性陳述之義務，這些陳述僅於作出之日為準。本公司提醒讀者，前瞻性陳述並非未來表現之保證，實際結果可能與前瞻性陳述中預期、預測或假設之結果有重大差異。可能導致本公司實際結果與前瞻性陳述中預期結果有重大差異之重要因素已於下文列示。請參閱本年度報告開頭之「前瞻性陳述警示」。
下列所討論之一或多項風險之發生，可能對本公司之業務、前景、財務狀況、營運成果與現金流造成重大且不利之影響，您可能損失部分或全部之投資。下列風險依最適用之標題分類，但這些風險亦可能與其他標題相關。此外， herein 所述之風險因素並非本公司可能面對之全部風險，且可能有其他尚未為本公司所知或本公司目前認為不重要或普遍適用於所有美國營運公司之風險，這些風險可能出現或變得重要。

一般而言，我們的保險政策的 premium rates 是在投保時建立的，因此在所有基礎成本皆為已知之前。和其他 workers' compensation 保險公司一樣，我們在設定 premium rates 時依賴估計與假設。建立足夠的 premium rates 是必要的，以產生足夠的 revenue 來抵銷損失、損失調整費用及其他承保費用，並賺取承保利潤。如果我們未能準確評估風險，我們可能未能收取足夠的 premium rates 來覆蓋我們的損失與費用，這可能會降低我們的 net income，並導致我們無利可圖。例如，在為新投保人啟動投保時，我們會根據投保人先前保險電信業者提供的 prior claims 資訊，來估計未來的 claims 費用。如果這些 prior claims 資訊不正確，我們可能因使用過低的 claims 估計值而低估我們的保單。結果，我們為投保人提供保險覆蓋的實際成本，可能顯著高於我們收取的 premium。
